title: Edmund and the Well
premise: Felix Eastwick, a skeptical urban explorer who documents unmapped tunnels beneath the drowned town of Coldharbour Fen, is hired to survey an excavation site where workers have uncovered a door sealed from the inside. When a crew member vanishes and frost blooms in impossible patterns across the concrete, Felix realizes the tunnels were never empty—they were a prison, and the excavation was an invitation. As the thing below hunts by cold and memory, Felix must ally with the diggers' ostracized foreman and a local archivist whose family helped seal the well generations ago. In the end, Felix learns survival demands a price: someone must take the old keeper's place behind the door, and justice outside the law means choosing who pays—ending with Felix sealing himself inside at dawn, leaving his found family above to guard the pattern.
about_author: A. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former hydrological surveyor who spent a decade mapping drainage systems beneath English fen towns before turning to fiction. They write horror rooted in infrastructure—the dread of what civic blueprints quietly omit.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He maps storm drains beneath Coldharbour Fen for money and anonymity, documenting a tunnel branch absent from every official survey. His emotional beat is controlled detachment—he photographs everything, believes nothing. A chalk mark on the tunnel wall, fresh and deliberate, unsettles him more than he admits.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Hired by Halloway Excavation to survey their site, he inspects a stone door unearthed forty feet down, its bolts thrown from within. Foreman Dana Okafor dismisses his unease; night watchman Pietro jokes about knocking. The chapter ends with frost forming on the door's inner face—where no air should move.

chapters.title: What Pietro Heard
chapters.summary: Pietro's POV. Alone on night shift, he hears scratching that matches his own movements a half-second late, then a voice reciting names—including his grandmother's. He flees without clocking out. The emotional beat is creeping self-doubt: he can't tell what he heard from what he fears hearing.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Chasing records, he finds Maren Voss, town archivist, whose family ledger lists 'well-keepers' back to 1740—each entry ending with a date and the word 'invited.' She warns him the frost patterns are signatures, not weather. Felix's skepticism cracks; the beat is reluctant inheritance of a truth he didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Coldharbour Rules
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. A worker is found frozen solid in July, doors locked from inside. Company lawyers push to bury the incident; Dana refuses, forging reports to buy time instead of silence—an act of justice outside the law. The beat is her choosing conscience over career, aligning her with Felix and Maren.

chapters.title: The Pattern Writes Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Frost on the site office windows forms the ledger's keeper-names in sequence, ending with FELIX. He realizes the entity selects those who've seen the door. Maren explains the ritual: a keeper must be invited willingly or it takes everyone. The beat is terror converting into grim responsibility.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation—Felix, Dana, Maren. They fortify the site through one night, salt lines and iron bolts, holding until sunrise as the cold hunts them room by room. Pietro returns to help and is taken. The beat is found family forged under siege, and the cost made visible.

chapters.title: Invitation
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The entity offers a bargain through the frost: give it a willing keeper and release the rest. Maren claims the duty by bloodright, but Felix discovers the ledger's fine print—the keeper needn't be a Voss, only a volunteer who has read the names aloud. The beat is betrayal of expectation turned sacrifice.

chapters.title: Behind the Door
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the threshold, he reads the full roll of keepers, adding his own name, and the door unbolts inward. What waits isn't monstrous so much as patient and starving—a thing imprisoned by consent. The climax: Felix steps through, Dana throws the bolts from outside, and the frost stops mid-pattern.

chapters.title: Guardians of the Pattern
chapters.summary: Dana and Maren's alternating POV, months later. The site is a memorial; the company buried, exposed by Dana's forged-turned-honest testimony. Each winter they check the frost on Felix's old window: a single signature, calm, renewed. The resolution holds grief and purpose together—survival was bought, and they intend to be worth the price.
